Selection Model

Source: R/priors.R
selection_model.Rd

Declare the contextual sources retained by a selection model, how estimate weights combine, and a publication-group column for best-p-value selection when needed.

Usage

selection_model(
  estimate_random_effects = "integrate",
  other_random_effects = "condition",
  known_sampling_variance = "integrate",
  weight_rule = "product",
  group = NULL
)

Arguments

estimate_random_effects

Either "condition" or "integrate" (default), for the declared estimate-level true-effect source. One-to-one grouping determines this role in multivariate models; it does not imply independent covariance.

other_random_effects

Either "condition" (default) or "integrate", for all remaining declared random-effect terms.

known_sampling_variance

Either "condition" or "integrate" (default), for the complete sampling-error vector \(e \sim N(0,V)\). Conditioning retains its realized value during selection normalization; integration uses the full sampling covariance. This choice also applies to univariate and independent sampling errors supplied through vi or sei. It does not change V.

weight_rule

Either "product" (default), which multiplies estimate weights without publication grouping, or "best", which uses the weight at the smallest p-value within each publication group.

group

Optional unresolved data-column name, supplied as a bare name, a backtick-quoted name, or one character string. Active only for weight_rule = "best", where the default NULL requests automatic group resolution when data are bound. Product models ignore this argument and require no group column.

Value

A selection_model object containing fixed mode choices and a deferred column name or NULL. The group is used only by the best rule.

Details

This is RoBMA's re-export of BayesTools::selection_model(). The specification is stored in prior_weightfunction(model = ...). Constructor selection = selection_model(...) settings apply only to generated default priors; explicit priors retain their own specification. A group name is captured without evaluating data; RoBMA binds it only for weight_rule = "best". When group = NULL, best-rule groups come from a supported constructor's cluster input or, for independent models without a random structure, one group per estimate. Other best-rule models require an explicit group column. Conditioned sources remain unknown and estimated. Integrating estimate variation is the default; conditioning on it defines a different selection model. The specialized clustered interface retains its total heterogeneity, allocation and within-/between-cluster I2 summaries.

With positive sampling standard errors, the sampling law can be written as \(e = Sz\), with \(z \sim N(0,R)\) and \(V = SRS\), where \(S\) contains sampling standard errors and \(R\) is their correlation matrix. Conditioning retains all of \(e\); no residual sampling error is integrated separately. Covariance factorizations affect computation, not the selection model. Selection thresholds continue to use the original sampling standard errors.

When all outcome-generating sources are conditioned upon and weights are positive almost surely, selection weights cancel and the observed law is the ordinary Gaussian model. The likelihood then contains no information about the selection weights. A retained context with zero acceptance probability cannot complete the selection process. Integrating all sources instead gives population-level selection among completed studies. These choices are independent of prediction's conditioning_depth. Non-unit observation weights require known_sampling_variance = "integrate"; unit weights are equivalent to omitting weights. Other observation-weight restrictions still apply.

weight_rule = "best" uses the weight of the smallest p-value's bin, rather than the largest weight. weight_rule = "product" multiplies all estimate weights. Its joint normalizer retains the dependencies in the integrated covariance, regardless of grouping. In ensembles, only best-rule branches require matching publication partitions; product-only ensembles accept group = NULL.

See bselmodel.mv() for the supported conditioning cells, source and group requirements, and covariance boundaries.

See also

prior_weightfunction, bselmodel.mv(), RoBMA.mv()

Examples

prior_weightfunction(
  steps = .05,
  model = selection_model(known_sampling_variance = "condition")
)
#> omega[one-sided: .05] ~ CumDirichlet(1, 1)
#> Selection model:
#>   Estimate random effects: integrate (average effects before normalization).
#>   Other random effects: condition (retain unknown effects during normalization).
#>   Known sampling error: condition (retain full unknown error vector during normalization).
#>   Weight rule: product (Product of estimate weights).
#>   Group: unused for the product rule.
#>   Sources are resolved when model data are bound.
prior_weightfunction(
  steps = .05,
  model = selection_model(weight_rule = "best", group = paper_id)
)
#> omega[one-sided: .05] ~ CumDirichlet(1, 1)
#> Selection model:
#>   Estimate random effects: integrate (average effects before normalization).
#>   Other random effects: condition (retain unknown effects during normalization).
#>   Known sampling error: integrate (average full error vector before normalization).
#>   Weight rule: best (Weight of the best p-value).
#>   Group: 'paper_id' (unresolved data column).
#>   Sources are resolved when model data are bound.
